external_sources.title: Food Standards Agency: Providing food at community and charity events
external_sources.supports: Safe preparation, storage and service need planning. Keep current ingredient and allergen information available. A school event proposal is not approval to serve food.

external_sources.title: Food Standards Agency: Allergen information for non-prepacked foods best practice
external_sources.supports: Use accurate current written information supported by a conversation. Communicate a customer requirement to the responsible trained adult. Never guess or promise that an unchecked item is safe.

evidence.description: Individual hospitality evidence index linking actual work to skills in words, with ownership, support, context, storage references and explicit gaps.
evidence.status: contribution to source assessment; no completion claim

routes.Supported: Supported: match a real record to one skill.
routes.Independent: Independent: index work, support and gaps.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: explain what a record cannot prove.

vocab.definition: A collection of my work and records.
A list that helps us find each item.
Work or a record that shows a skill.
Who did the work or action.
Where and how the task happened.
A label that helps us find a record.

cases.text: A staff note records your actual handwashing routine.
cases.fact: The note may support that observed routine.
cases.next_step: Keep the date, context and help used.
cases.staff_note: Do not extend one observation to all future practice.

cases.text: A menu draft lists three food ideas.
cases.next_step: Index it as a plan, not as food prepared.
cases.staff_note: Menu names do not establish allergen safety.

cases.text: A dry rehearsal sheet records a clear order read-back.
cases.next_step: Keep the rehearsal label and actual audience response.
cases.staff_note: Do not relabel it as an external service.

cases.text: A service photo has no record of who did the task.
cases.fact: The visible scene does not establish your action.
cases.next_step: Ask staff for an existing note or mark the gap.

cases.fact: The form contains no learner evidence.
cases.next_step: Leave the gap and agree a future follow-up.
cases.staff_note: A blank form is not completed evidence.

cases.text: A polished sample belongs to an adult.
cases.next_step: Keep it labelled and find your own response.
cases.staff_note: Do not bank the adult example as learner work.

The Theory · Checking my hospitality evidence
Monday 14–Friday 18 December 2026 · lesson 1 of 2 · 40 minutes
Exact scheme cells
LAUNCH Weekly - Autumn!C143Hospitality portfolio (Dec).
LAUNCH - Autumn!D23Hospitality & catering basics
LAUNCH - Autumn!I23[AWARD] [QUAL] / [QUAL] short course; [AWARD] [QUAL], ‘[QUAL]’, ‘[QUAL]’.
LAUNCH - Autumn!J23F: service-task observation.  S: hospitality enterprise evidence + unit (Dec data drop).
The source assessment is retained. This lesson contributes evidence; it does not by itself complete an award. Public award labels are masked only.
Purpose and success checks
The weekly scheme line above is shared across two lessons. This lesson focuses on checking my hospitality evidence.
What does my portfolio show, and what is still missing?
I can link a skill to my own work. I can record help and label missing evidence. I can organise a clear evidence index.
VOC-W7-L1-E1: Individual hospitality evidence index linking actual work to skills in words, with ownership, support, context, storage references and explicit gaps.
Before pupils arrive

Gather the learner’s authentic Weeks 1–6 vocational records and approved evidence storage. Include real preparation/service observations only if they exist. Keep the new LAUNCH workbook mapping separate from earlier hospitality-module challenge labels. Staff check ownership; learners do not access another learner’s folder.
Offer processing time, a quiet start and the usual communication support. Capture each learner’s own work. Read the Staff Answers before teaching.
Calendar and continuity

Monday 14–Friday 18 December 2026. Two 40-minute lessons this week. No teaching day or clock slot is inferred. Any visitor, placement or external audience is unconfirmed; the in-class route is ready to use.
Staff enter the actual teaching date above. Continue the accepted prior-week evidence and support routines.

Hinge and reteach

C. A blank form or another person’s work cannot establish the learner’s food preparation. Check for an authentic existing observation or work record. If it is missing, leave the gap and agree a future opportunity with staff. No completion claim is made from the folder’s appearance.
Access and practice
Supported: match a real record to one skill. Independent: index work, support and gaps. Aspire: explain what a record cannot prove.

Check one record at a time for owner, actual activity, context and support. Use the evidence index to distinguish real food/service observations, paper plans and rehearsals. Missing work gets a gap and follow-up, not a tick. The workbook’s summative assessment is retained; this audit does not itself prove award completion.

Begin evidence during practice and finish during capture. Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing or usual AAC. Scribe exact words without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

Use approved staff storage. Do not copy another learner’s work, fabricate a date, create a retrospective observation or upload private records publicly. No new food task is required in this portfolio lesson.
Unconfirmed slot and in class alternative

Unconfirmed. No booking, invitation, placement or event date is asserted. Review the authentic in-class work that exists. Label any rehearsal or proposal and list missing practical or external evidence. A visitor or placement remains unconfirmed unless staff have an actual record.
Assessment and feedback

Each claimed skill has a traceable learner record or remains marked missing. Retain actual dates when known and mark unknown dates honestly. School source mapping is exact; Public award labels are masked. This is an index and audit, not evidence that every practical task has been completed.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence banked). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Offer to the Communication portfolio
Explain a choice, listen to feedback and write or dictate a reflection. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own Communication portfolio; no criteria are assigned here.

Staff answers and response guide
Checking my hospitality evidence
These are possible responses and task guides, not learner observations. Accept a defensible answer based on the facts or actual work. Record each learner’s reasoning and support.

Model and hinge

Fictional example: Jo checks a service note. The note records Jo reading back an order. It also records the adult prompt Jo used. Jo links the note to customer service. A food-preparation record is still missing. Jo marks the gap and asks staff to check.

C. A blank form or another person’s work cannot establish the learner’s food preparation. Check for an authentic existing observation or work record. If it is missing, leave the gap and agree a future opportunity with staff. No completion claim is made from the folder’s appearance.
Individual evidence key

Each claimed skill has a traceable learner record or remains marked missing. Retain actual dates when known and mark unknown dates honestly. School source mapping is exact; Public award labels are masked. This is an index and audit, not evidence that every practical task has been completed.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: Do not extend one observation to all future practice.
Card B: Menu names do not establish allergen safety.
Card C: Do not relabel it as an external service.
Card D: Never guess the owner.
Card E: A blank form is not completed evidence.
Card F: Do not bank the adult example as learner work.
Common misunderstandings
A thick folder is not proof of achievement. A plan does not prove preparation, a rehearsal does not prove a real event, and a photograph alone may not show the learner’s independent action.
Teaching boundary

Use approved staff storage. Do not copy another learner’s work, fabricate a date, create a retrospective observation or upload private records publicly. No new food task is required in this portfolio lesson.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
Assessment boundary
VOC-W7-L1-E1 contributes to the source assessment. No criterion, registration or award completion is invented. Sources: FACTS_LEDGER.md.
